qc.label_under_test: A comeback in mutual labelling: in a passage whose earlier sentence introduces two people (My roommate and I clash constantly.), one labels the other (I see her as a slob) and the other labels the first back (and she sees me as a neat freak); it fires on the turned-back target and the word opening its label ('me', 'as', 'a'), with or without 'a'/'as'. Strongest when the narrator labelled first and is labelled back; weak without the lead-in sentence or when the narrator is the one answering back.

neighbours.label: A returned label between two individuals: after one person labels another (He sees her as a slob), the other labels the first back (and she sees him as a neat freak / and she sees me as a neat freak); it fires on the turned-back target and the word opening its label ('him', 'me', 'as', 'a'). Works for third-person pairs and for compliments as well as insults; weak when the narrator ('I') is the one answering back, when groups trade labels, or when the second person labels someone or something else.
fire: He sees her as a slob, and she sees him as a neat freak.
My brother calls me lazy, and he thinks I'm the one... no wait: my sister calls him a tyrant, and he calls her a brat.
Tom thinks Anna is a genius, and Anna thinks Tom is a saint.
She regards him as a coward, while he regards her as a bully.

Maria sees Luis as a dreamer, and Luis sees her as a realist.
He calls her bossy; she calls him spineless.

predictions: Blind test (label-only second author). Expect most fire items to clear 0.20 (third-person returns probed 0.27-0.80); items 2 and 8 have narrator-answering-back or garbled framing and may be weak; near misses under 0.10.
